book.title: Bits and Questions
book.kicker: A sample book for readers who can count
book.lead: How many yes or no questions does it take to find one thing? This sample answers that for equally likely items and then for skewed odds, and shows every part of the format once.
book.goal: Compute the average number of questions an optimal guesser needs
book.emphasis: Reason from a skewed menu to the question order, and check any count by halving

questions.text: How many yes or no questions find one of N equally likely items?
questions.answer: log2 N, because each answer can halve the candidates.

questions.text: How few questions are needed on average when the odds are skewed?
questions.answer: The entropy: each outcome costs its surprisal, averaged by probability.

concepts.gloss: The information in one yes or no answer between equally likely options.
Asking questions that split the remaining candidates in half.
The bits an outcome of probability p costs: minus log2 p.
Average surprisal: the fewest questions per outcome on average.
